page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, with 24 physical cores and a 1:1 thread-to-core allocation. The instance is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and CPU-based processing. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates solid compute capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1437.29 and a multi-core score of 23003.67. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which assist in vector calculations and neural network inference. This is reflected in the LLM inference benchmarks, where the instance achieves 1275.25 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 34.41 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. Memory performance shows a read-only small block bandwidth of 1277.1 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 36.67 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.hfc6.6xlarge is its compute-heavy memory ratio of 1:2 and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed make it a viable option for workloads that require consistent compute performance without the overhead of hyperthreading. It is well-suited for compute-intensive tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, static web serving, and high-throughput database operations, as demonstrated by its 21.93 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This hardware profile is optimized for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and database operations where dedicated CPU resources are required.
